svg.title: Bennett Family · Three-Generation Genogram
svg.desc: A clinical three-generation family genogram. The top row is the grandparents, Harold (deceased 2016, marked with a cross through his square) and Margaret, married in 1965. Their two children are Daniel and Susan. Daniel married Karen in 2005 and divorced her in 2016 — the double slash on their line — and their two children, Chloe and Ethan, hang from that union's own sibship line. Daniel remarried Priya in 2018 and their son Ravi hangs from the second union, so no child is attached to the wrong parents. Squares are male, circles female; a number inside a shape is that person's current age and the deceased carry their dates instead. Shading marks a diagnosed condition, placed as McGoldrick places it: the bottom half in amber for alcohol use disorder in Harold and Daniel, the left half in indigo for depression in Chloe, who is the index person and therefore drawn with a second outline. Four emotional relationships are drawn by line form, not colour: three parallel lines from Karen to Chloe for fusion, two parallel lines between Chloe and Ethan for closeness, a red zigzag from Daniel to Chloe for conflict, and a red line broken in the middle with a bar at each end from Margaret to Susan for an emotional cutoff. The dashed rounded rectangle encloses the people who live in one home: Karen with Chloe and Ethan. A legend at the foot names every symbol used.
